rationale: ROUND 2 on correlation c48b7612. Round 1 returned REVISE on a gating objection from editquality (edit 8, the migration's `steps` vs `substeps` container key). Every objection is answered below, and SIX of them changed the code. Round 1's plan described code that was partly unwritten; this round describes code that exists, compiles, and is under test — so several objections about missing symbols are answered by pointing at them. === ANSWERS TO ROUND 1, objection by objection === 1. editquality edit 8 HIGH — 'sub_workflow may key its running half as `substeps`, not `steps`'. ANSWERED BY THE COUNCIL'S OWN READ-ONLY CHECK in round 1: has_substeps=false, has_steps=true on the live page-content-writer row. The seat was right to demand the check and right that the RAISE would not have caught it — so the migration now ALSO anchors on the container: its WHERE reads `#>> '{...,sub_workflow,steps,generate_content,action}' = 'execute_llm_prompt'`, which is 0 rows and a loud RAISE if the container key is ever anything but `steps`. The check is in the migration, not in a canary. 2. editquality edit 8 MEDIUM — '497 may already be taken'. CORRECT, AND IT WAS. Another session took 497 between the plan and the write. The file is now 509_writer_rewrites_define_by_negation_HOLD.sql. Verified against the directory at write time; the highest number in the tree was 508. 3. bug_historian + guardian edit 5 MEDIUM — 'ScanContentDataForNegation is undefined; nothing traverses a nested content map'. CORRECT AT ROUND 1. It is now a named edit (edit 2) with its own file and tests: WalkContentStrings recurses maps, lists and lists-of-objects, returns a stable sorted order (Go map order would make field paths unstable — bugs_open/327's defect in miniature), SKIPS non-prose fields by name and by value shape so a URL is never sent to a model as a sentence, and carries a Set closure so a repair writes THROUGH to the map the renderer reads rather than into a rebuilt copy. Four tests, including the negative arm (cta_url, stat_1_value, icon, items[0].url must not be walked). 4. guardian edit 6 MEDIUM — 'the new action is never registered in GlobalActionRegistry'. CORRECT AT ROUND 1, now registered (edit 5's sketch shows the entry). Also covered by registry_parity_test.go, which fails on a spec without a registry entry. 5. compliance edit 4 HIGH — 'nothing scans the accepted replacement for banned claims'. CORRECT, AND THE MOST VALUABLE OBJECTION OF THE ROUND. The acceptance test was purely structural, and 'say what it IS' is exactly the pressure that fills an affirmative slot with an invented superlative. Fixed: every candidate now goes through checkBannedClaims + loadEvidenceBase — the SAME implementation the meta-description gate uses, fleetWide=true so a site with no evidence register still gets the fleet arm — BEFORE the structural test, and a hit is a rejection with reason banned_claim_. 6. compliance edit 5 MEDIUM — 'the prompt should forbid new capability/reliability claims explicitly'. DONE, in the prompt text: 'Say only what the original sentence already supports... do not reach for a superlative to fill the gap the removed contrast leaves'. 7. llm_reliability edit 6 MEDIUM (truncation) — DONE, both arms: aiservice.IsTruncated on the error, and a usage check (output_tokens >= the max_tokens actually sent) for a provider that returns a cut answer as a 200. Either way it splices NOTHING and says so in the marker. Note the pre-existing safe direction too: a truncated JSON object does not parse, and an unparseable answer already spliced nothing. 8. llm_reliability edit 6 MEDIUM (where the model config comes from) — it reads exactly as ExecuteLLMPromptAction does: resolveAIServiceConfig(agentConfig, stepConfig, stepName) then createAIClient, so the root/step overlay semantics are shared rather than re-invented, and the effective model is visible in llm_call_log.model for rows marked 'RETRY (bugs_open/305'. 9. render_guardian edit 6 LOW — 'tag multiset equality does not guarantee nesting'. CORRECT: 'x' and 'x' have identical multisets. Changed to tag-SEQUENCE equality, with a test asserting the inverted-nesting case is rejected and the well-formed one accepted. 10. reuse_agent + prior_art_librarian edit 6 — 'why not extend the bugs_open/119 re-ask, or reuse apply_section_edit?' MEASURED, not argued. (a) apply_section_edit REQUIRES a page_component_id — it edits a persisted page_components row and reassembles the page (its header: 'Performs the edit on a page_components row'). At this seam the section is being BORN; no row exists until save_page_sections runs, so there is nothing for it to apply to. It is the right mechanism one stage later, which is where copy-editor uses it. (b) The 119 re-ask fires ONLY when a JSON-declaring step produced an answer that will not parse; its contract is 'one chance to be readable', and it re-asks for the WHOLE section — the shape measured at ~5x the cost and able to lose a required field. Extending it would conflate 'unusable answer' with 'usable answer we want changed'. They do stack (both can fire on one section), and that is stated as a cost, not hidden. 11. prior_art_librarian edit 6 HIGH — 'nothing sits between generate_content and render_section is an asserted absence'. ANSWERED BY THE COUNCIL'S OWN CHECK in round 1: gen_next = render_section on the live row, i.e. adjacent with no intermediate step. 12. prior_art_librarian edit 6 MEDIUM — 'execute_llm_prompt has no ActionInputSpec is unverified'. VERIFIED: scripts/audit-optional-key-budget.sh lists it under 'NOT COUNTED — no ActionInputSpec, so the optional surface is UNKNOWABLE, not zero', with 66 carriers. The new action declares its own spec and now appears in that report at 1 optional key; the cron literal was regenerated in the same commit because the parity test caught it at 0 against a declared 1. 13. debug_historian edit 6 MEDIUM — 'no rollback file'. CORRECT AT ROUND 1: 509_writer_rewrites_define_by_negation_HOLD_ROLLBACK.sql now exists, and its ORDER is load-bearing (re-point first, then delete the step; the other order leaves a chain naming a step that no longer exists). 14. debug_historian edit 6 MEDIUM — 'two active rows for one agent type'. ANSWERED BY THE COUNCIL'S OWN CHECK: page-content-writer count = 1. The verify block counts POSITIVE presence and requires exactly 1, so a second row would raise rather than pass. 15. editquality edit 7 + bug_historian edit 7 MEDIUM — 'the per-page budget's cross-iteration state is unproven; make the canary a gating precondition'. ACCEPTED AND ADOPTED: the migration's header now names the canary as a PRECONDITION of applying it, alongside the image check. The file is _HOLD, so this is enforceable rather than aspirational — renaming it out of _HOLD is the deliberate act, and it now has two conditions rather than one. The degradation if the assumption is false is stated and safe (per-section budget, headlines still repaired). 16. architecture edit 5 LOW — 'a default-on key on a shared action becomes a de facto contract'. Noted in the concept-register entry (CQ-026) in the same commit: copy_gate_findings has NO consumer today, and a second reader of it needs an ActionInputSpec governing the key. === THE UNCHANGED CORE, restated because seats have no cross-round memory === bugs_open/305: the owner read three live pages, quoted two sentences built on define-by-negation, and ruled that this copy must never leave the framework again. The rule already exists in the house voice and does not hold — migration 228 shipped it and its own header records that it 'did not work', and the fleet_copy_quality ablation concluded 'a rule can only name a form; what goes wrong is an instinct'. The only wired detector (voicetells.go strawmanCommaRe) needs a trailing ', but' and matches 23 of 1,503 sections — neither of the owner's sentences. So: the family as one shared scanner, counted unconditionally at the render and compile seams, and repaired at the writer seam by replacing SENTENCES under a per-page budget, with every replacement judged against a displacement set because 'keep whichever scores lower' rewards 'X instead of Y'.

plan.summary: Round 2. Add the define-by-negation family as one pure shared scanner and a content-map walker; make the existing voice gate use them; count the construction on every rendered LLM section and every compiled page (annotation only, default ON); and add a registered action that repairs the sentences beyond a per-PAGE budget of two, or any in a headline field, by splicing model-supplied replacements that must pass a claim-safety scan, a displacement check and a fact-preservation check. Enabled on one agent by a HELD migration. Plus the brief-side daily check that covers the gap the gate deliberately leaves.

edits.rationale: The family, pure and shared by every consumer so they cannot disagree about what the fault IS. Five shapes, each hit naming its containing SENTENCE with offsets into the RAW field value (a repair splices by exact substring; a sentence recovered from stripped text is not a substring of its field). ScanContrastNeighbours is a SEPARATE class that can never trip and only rejects a rewrite — without it a repair passes by moving the problem. NegationExempt is SENTENCE-scoped against brief-supplied text only, because 'rather than' is in every rendered writer prompt. AcceptNegationRewrite fails CLOSED. ROUND 2: tag comparison is now by SEQUENCE, not multiset (render_guardian: inverted nesting keeps every tag and is malformed); negative_reveal is third-person only, because the first-person form flagged 'we do not offer refunds', a policy statement the writer's own STRICT RULE 19 asks for.
edits.sketch: shapes: x_not_y | not_x_but_y | staccato | rather_than | negative_reveal neighbours (reject-only): instead_of | more_than_just | isnt_just | unlike | as_opposed_to | em_dash | … AcceptNegationRewrite(from, to, protectFrom) -> (bool, reason) empty|unchanged|gutted|ballooned|still_|displaced_|dropped_figure|invented_figure| dropped_link|markup_changed|invented_name -func sameTagMultiset(a,b) // counts equal is NOT markup preserved +func sameTagSequence(a,b) // order-equal; rejects x protectFrom = the construction's offset: facts BEFORE it are the claim and must survive; facts after it are the contrasted alternative the rewrite exists to drop.

edits.rationale: ROUND 2, and it answers bug_historian's and guardian's edit-5 objection directly: this is the traversal that was undefined at round 1. One walker for both consumers, because a repair that scanned a different set of fields from the annotation produces a count nobody can reconcile with what was fixed. It decides what counts as prose in ONE place (a cta_url or a stat value is not a sentence), returns a SORTED order because Go map order would make field paths unstable, and carries a Set closure so a repair writes through to the live map rather than into a rebuilt copy — the silent-no-op shape, designed out rather than guarded.
edits.sketch:
type NegationTextField struct { Path string; Text string; Set func(string) }
WalkContentStrings(map) []NegationTextField   // recurses maps, lists, lists-of-objects; sorted
prosey(): skips (^|_)(url|href|id|slug|class|icon|colour|value|price|email|phone|…)$, bare tokens, paths
ScanContentDataForNegation(map) []map[string]any  // field, shape, matched, sentence, headline
IsHeadlineField("items[2].heading") == true      // last segment, index-stripped

edits.rationale: The existing strawman arm was blind to the shape the owner complained about; it now calls the shared scanner, so the post-deploy voice check and the meta-description gate inherit the family. ONE finding per SHAPE per block carrying that shape's count — per-hit findings would flag almost every page and tell a human nothing. 'rather than' is excluded from the per-hit path and becomes a page-level DENSITY (contrast_density, default 2, long-form 4) mirroring triad_density, because it is present in 43% of sections while the house voice permits a contrasting pair once or twice per page.

The COUNT goes where it cannot be forgotten: the repair is opt-in and runs on one agent, so every other writer's fault must still be visible or the fleet figure is whatever the wired agents happen to produce. 'A gate a workflow author can forget to wire is a comment.' Annotation only — it adds result keys and changes nothing else, passes errors through untouched, and is silent on clean copy. The PAGE count re-scans each section's content_data rather than summing the per-section annotations, so a template-rendered section is still counted and a sum cannot read zero the day the metadata extractor stops forwarding a key. Wrapping at the registry rather than editing inside the two actions is deliberate: v3_site_actions.go is a 6,000-line file several sessions edit concurrently, and on 2026-08-20 it carried another session's uncommitted work referencing symbols absent at HEAD — a pathspec commit takes same-file passengers, so an inline hunk would have broken the compile at HEAD for every session. Verified by grep that nothing else in the repo calls either action directly.

The repair, as its own registered action with its own input spec — not a key on execute_llm_prompt, which has 66 carriers and no spec (so the RFC_022 budget cannot see keys added to it) and also serves council seats and classifiers. ROUND 2 adds the two guards the council asked for: every candidate replacement goes through checkBannedClaims + loadEvidenceBase (the meta-description gate's own implementation, fleet arm ON) BEFORE the structural test, because 'say what it IS' is exactly the pressure that invents a superlative and nothing downstream inspects a spliced sentence for claim content; and a truncated repair splices NOTHING, detected both by aiservice.IsTruncated and by output_tokens reaching the max_tokens actually sent. Config resolution is ExecuteLLMPromptAction's own (resolveAIServiceConfig → createAIClient), so root/step overlay semantics are shared rather than re-invented.

The entire enablement surface. ROUND 2 changes: renumbered 497 → 509 (497 was taken, exactly as editquality suspected); the WHERE now anchors on the CONTAINER path ...sub_workflow,steps,... so a row keyed `substeps` matches 0 rows and RAISEs rather than inserting a step nothing runs (the round-1 gating objection, which the council's own check answered as has_steps=true — the anchor makes it enforced rather than observed); a separate _HOLD_ROLLBACK file exists, with its order load-bearing (re-point first, then delete); and the header now names TWO preconditions for un-holding it, the image AND the cross-iteration budget canary. It is _HOLD because it rewires the step CHAIN: applied before the image, every section build fails at an unknown action.

The half the gate cannot do. The gate EXEMPTS anything the site's brief supplied — a site's voice specification outranks the fleet rules — and that is precisely the route the owner's complaint arrived by: the complained-of tagline reaches the writer in 1,369 prompts and returns in 409 responses. This asks daily whether a brief HANDS the writer such a phrase, over the writer-visible surface derived at RUNTIME from the live prompt's own {{.site_specs.specs.*}} references — never data::text, which is ~4x the text the writer reads and which made an earlier fleet census wrong by 2x. Three classes kept apart: supplied (files a finding), instructional (counted only — transfer is UNMEASURED), regulatory (left alone, by calling the SAME NegationExempt the gate uses, so the two halves cannot send a human in opposite directions). LIVE and proven: 10 of 25 sites, and the close-out arm closed two sites on positive re-observation.

visibleSurface(liveWriterConfig) -> [content_direction.formatted, identity.key_differentiators, …]
assess(): supplied {quoted | list_item} + mandated PER BLOCK (a whole-field test marks every phrase
          in a 15k-char brief as mandated: fleet count 8 -> 4 when scoped correctly)

  (NOT DO UPDATE: trg_site_work_items_updated_at + the stale reaper = bugs_closed/213's immortal item)
writeDocNote on EVERY run, clean included; exit 0/1/2, and REFUSE on an empty surface or empty census

edits.rationale: The new item_type is classified in the same commit that mints it, per that guard's standing obligation — a type this file cannot see is a type whose completions nobody records a choice about. catJudgement rather than catMechanical, and the entry says why: the re-observation IS mechanical (the phrase is either in the visible surface or it is not, and the detector performs it), but whether the phrase SHOULD go is the site owner's judgement.

"brief_supplies_negation": {catJudgement, "a site's writer-visible brief HANDS the writer a phrase built on define-by-negation … the remedy is the SITE OWNER editing their own brief, and the writer-seam gate exempts brief-supplied phrases precisely because a site's voice specification outranks the fleet rules"},

plan.risks:
1. DISPLACEMENT ADOPTED SILENTLY — the failure that would make this worse than nothing. Mitigated by per-replacement rejection against the neighbour set, with every rejection logged WITH ITS REASON. Residual: the same instinct in a grammar nobody listed. A reviewer should read the neighbour list for a shape it misses.
2. AN OVERCLAIM SPLICED IN — round 1's compliance objection. Now gated by the estate's own banned-claims scan with the fleet arm on. Residual: an overclaim no pattern names. The prompt also forbids new capability claims explicitly, which is a rule and therefore weak on its own; the scan is the control.
3. THE PER-PAGE BUDGET'S CROSS-ITERATION STATE IS UNPROVEN AT RUNTIME. Now an explicit PRECONDITION in the held migration's header rather than a follow-up canary. Degrades to per-section (headlines still repaired) if false.
4. THE 43% ARM MAY BE TOO BROAD. 'rather than' is either a real fleet tic or too wide a pattern. It is a DENSITY in the post-deploy check for that reason, and the rejection log settles it within a week of traffic. The owning lane has been asked directly.
5. COST: ~43% of sections re-asked once at ~$0.0135 (the patch shape), ~$1.2-1.7/day at 215 sections/day; with the 119 re-ask also firing, up to three calls on one section. If anyone converts this back to a whole-section re-ask it becomes ~$200/month and materially slower builds.
6. WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO: it will not clean the three pages the owner named — their tagline is brief-supplied and exempt BY DESIGN — and it holds five named FORMS rather than promising the instinct is gone. Both are stated to the owner and to the three affected lanes, in writing, before any code shipped.
